1	# Claude Code Background Sessions Scope
2	
3	## 1. Problem
4	
5	The Control Room already hosts a native supervisor surface for OpenCode:
6	`admin/opencode_client.py` talks to the running OpenCode server, and
7	`scripts/supervise.py` relays native sessions into the Control Room's
8	Redis-backed event streams and flags stalled/off-track work for human review.
9	There is no equivalent surface for Claude Code's own background-session
10	mechanism.
11	
12	`src/instrument/claude_adapter.py` drives the `claude` CLI today, but only in
13	headless, single-shot mode: `run_claude_agentic` builds one
14	`claude -p "<prompt>" --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions
15	[--model ...]` subprocess, streams its `stream-json` events through
16	`ClaudeStreamAdapter`, and returns when that one process exits
17	[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:236-346]. It never enumerates, attaches to,
18	or controls a `claude --bg` background session, and it maps the framework's
19	advisor-model id `claude-fable-5` to `claude-sonnet-5` for the primary model
20	[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:185-211] — Claude Code's own
21	`--advisor fable` server-side advisor is a distinct mechanism, unused today.
22	
23	Claude Code separately ships a background-session product: `claude --bg`
24	starts a supervised session that keeps running after the launching terminal
25	exits, `claude agents` lists and monitors those sessions, and `claude attach`,
26	`claude logs`, `claude stop`/`kill`, `claude respawn`, and `claude rm` manage
27	one session's lifecycle, all hosted by a `claude daemon` supervisor process.
28	None of this is visible from the Control Room. An operator who dispatches a
29	`claude --bg` task today has no fleet card, no transcript, and no lifecycle
30	controls inside the command rail — they have to shell out separately, which
31	is exactly the gap the OpenCode native surface already closed for OpenCode.
32	
33	This feature adds the Claude analog: list, observe, and lifecycle-control
34	`claude --bg` sessions and the `claude daemon` that hosts them, inside the
35	existing Control Room, reusing its command-rail aesthetic and SSE/Redis
36	transport rather than building a second dashboard.
37	
38	## 2. Investigated CLI Facts
39	
40	Investigated against the Claude Code CLI reference,
41	<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference>. Commands and flags below are
42	quoted from that reference; anything not stated there is called out as not
43	possible rather than inferred.
44	
45	### Starting a background session
46	
47	- `claude --bg "<task>"` / `claude --background "<task>"` — starts the task as
48	  a background agent and returns immediately, printing the session ID and
49	  management commands. Cannot be combined with `-p`/`--print`. Can combine
50	  with `--exec` to run a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude
51	  session, and with `--agent` to run a specific subagent.
52	- `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, when set on a `--bg` launch, persists
53	  across supervisor restarts for that session (i.e., a respawn keeps the
54	  original permission mode).
55	
56	### Listing / observing
57	
58	- `claude agents` — opens an interactive terminal "agent view" for monitoring
59	  and dispatching background sessions; **requires an interactive terminal**,
60	  so it is not something a Flask backend can drive headlessly.
61	- `claude agents --json` — prints active sessions as a JSON array, scriptable.
62	- `claude agents --json --all` — same, but includes completed background
63	  sessions.
64	- `claude agents --cwd <path>` — restricts the listing to sessions started
65	  under that directory.
66	- `claude logs <id>` — prints recent output from one background session. This
67	  is a plain, non-interactive stdout dump — safe to call headlessly and diff.
68	- `claude attach <id>` — attaches to a background session **in a terminal**
69	  to view and follow it live; the reference explicitly scopes this to
70	  "view/follow," not steering input, and — like `claude agents` — implies a
71	  real interactive TTY, not a scriptable stream.
72	- `claude daemon status` — prints the background-session supervisor's state,
73	  version, socket directory, and worker count; exits 1 if the supervisor
74	  isn't running.
75	
76	### Lifecycle control
77	
78	- `claude stop <id>` / `claude kill <id>` (`kill` is an alias for `stop`) —
79	  stops a background session.
80	- `claude respawn <id>` — restarts a background session, running or stopped,
81	  **with its conversation intact**. `claude respawn --all` restarts every
82	  running session (e.g., to pick up an updated Claude Code binary).
83	- `claude rm <id>` — removes a session from the list. The transcript is not
84	  deleted; it stays on disk and remains reachable via `claude --resume`.
85	- `claude daemon stop --any` — stops the background-session supervisor and
86	  every session it hosts. `--any` is required to confirm stopping an
87	  on-demand supervisor (the default supervisor kind). `--keep-workers` leaves
88	  the background sessions running so the next supervisor reconnects to them
89	  instead of killing them. This is the documented recovery path for an
90	  unresponsive supervisor.
91	
92	### Advisor
93	
94	- `--advisor <model>` (e.g. `--advisor fable`, `--advisor opus`,
95	  `--advisor sonnet`, or a full model ID) enables the server-side advisor tool
96	  for a session, and works with any session mode, including background
97	  (`claude --bg --advisor fable "task"`). `fable` requires Fable 5 access. It
98	  takes precedence over the `advisorModel` setting. This is a pass-through
99	  launch flag, not something the Control Room implements — it only needs to
100	  be exposed as an optional start-time input.
101	
102	### What is explicitly NOT possible
103	
104	The reference documents no way to send input to, or otherwise interactively
105	steer, a *running* background session. `attach` is view/follow only; there is
106	no `claude bg send`, no prompt-injection command, and no documented
107	`delivery: steer` equivalent to OpenCode's native
108	`POST /api/session/{id}/prompt` [contrast with admin/opencode_client.py:94-102].
109	Concretely:
110	
111	- **Interrupt has no direct analog.** OpenCode's `interrupt` stops active work
112	  *without* ending the session [admin/opencode_client.py:104-107]. Claude
113	  Code's closest primitives are `stop` (ends the session; conversation is
114	  preserved but the process is gone) and `respawn` (restarts the session with
115	  its conversation intact, effectively resuming after a stop). Neither is a
116	  live, in-flight interrupt-and-keep-running.
117	- **There is no send-input / steer control.** This spec deliberately does not
118	  invent one. Any control surface for background sessions is limited to the
119	  lifecycle verbs the CLI actually exposes: stop/kill, respawn, rm, and
120	  daemon stop.
121	- **`claude agents` and `claude attach` need a real TTY**, so this feature
122	  uses only the scriptable subset (`claude agents --json --all`,
123	  `claude logs <id>`, `claude daemon status`, and the lifecycle commands)
124	  driven via `subprocess`, the same way `claude_adapter.py` already drives the
125	  CLI for headless runs [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299].
126	
127	## 3. Chosen Integration Approach
128	
129	### Decision
130	
131	Add a small `admin/claude_agents_client.py` subprocess wrapper around the
132	scriptable `claude` subcommands above (list, start, logs, stop, respawn, rm,
133	daemon status), mirroring the shape of `OpenCodeClient`
134	[admin/opencode_client.py] but calling a CLI instead of an HTTP API. Add a
135	lightweight poller (module-level thread or endpoint-triggered refresh, not a
136	new always-on service) that periodically runs `claude agents --json --all` to
137	refresh a Redis-cached roster, and — for the currently selected/attached
138	session only — diffs `claude logs <id>` output and republishes new lines
139	through the existing `LivePublisher` event/log channel used by
140	`instrument/live.py`, under a distinct `cell_id` namespace (e.g.
141	`claude_bg_<session-id>`). The existing `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` SSE
142	endpoint, its retained-history replay, and its `replay_complete` boundary
143	[admin/server.py:450-490] then serve the transcript with zero new SSE
144	machinery. Add new `POST`-mutating endpoints for start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon
145	actions, all behind the loopback + JSON + Idempotency-Key guard the
146	design-session endpoints already enforce [admin/server.py:104-124, 127-178].
147	
148	The frontend gets one additive fleet section — "Claude background sessions"
149	— rendered with the same card list, selection, and transcript hand-off
150	pattern `selectCell`/`selectDesignSession` already use
151	[admin/static/app.js:721-796], not a new page or visual language. Lifecycle
152	buttons (Stop, Respawn, Rm) use the same `window.confirm`-gated pattern as the
153	existing Interrupt control [admin/static/app.js:1284-1300], and Detach stays
154	a browser-only `EventSource.close()` with no process effect
155	[admin/static/app.js:803-811].
156	
157	### Rationale
158	
159	- **Subprocess, not a new client library or service.** `claude_adapter.py`
160	  already resolves the CLI binary and drives it via subprocess for headless
161	  runs [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:36-46, 291-299]; there is no HTTP API
162	  for background sessions to call instead — the CLI *is* the contract. This
163	  keeps the pattern consistent with the one Claude Code integration this
164	  repo already has, and avoids adding a daemon RPC client that isn't
165	  documented.
166	- **`claude logs` polling instead of `claude attach`.** `attach` is
167	  documented as an interactive terminal follow, the same category as
168	  `claude agents`'s own "requires an interactive terminal" caveat. Wiring a
169	  no-TTY subprocess to `attach` risks it blocking on terminal I/O or emitting
170	  control codes meant for a real terminal. `logs` is a plain stdout dump,
171	  safe to call on an interval and diff — the same shape as
172	  `scripts/supervise.py`'s existing poll-and-relay loop
173	  [scripts/supervise.py:81-94, 158-176, 243-269], just polling a CLI command
174	  instead of an HTTP session.
175	- **Reuse the `cell_id`-namespaced relay-into-`/api/events/<cell_id>` pattern.**
176	  `scripts/supervise.py` already proves this pattern for OpenCode: it invents
177	  a readable `cell_id` per native session (`_cell_id_for`,
178	  [scripts/supervise.py:151-155]) and relays that session's events into the
179	  Control Room's existing Redis event log/channel so the frontend needs no
180	  new stream type [scripts/supervise.py:158-176]. Background Claude sessions
181	  do the same under a `claude_bg_` prefix, so `admin/server.py`'s SSE
182	  endpoint, replay boundary, and frontend transcript renderer need no changes.
183	- **No steer/send-input control, anywhere in the surface.** The CLI reference
184	  has no equivalent to OpenCode's `delivery: queue|steer` prompt admission
185	  [admin/opencode_client.py:94-102]. Inventing one (e.g. by piping into a
186	  wrapped subprocess's stdin) would control a mechanism the CLI doesn't
187	  document as supported and could silently corrupt session state. The
188	  Control Room's job here is Observe (list, logs, daemon status) and a
189	  narrow, confirmed Control (start, stop/kill, respawn, rm, daemon stop) —
190	  not steering.
191	- **Reuse the existing model-alias table and workdir-allowlist pattern.**
192	  Background-session start should call `_resolve_claude_model`
193	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] so a UI-selected model produces
194	  the exact same `--model` argument the headless adapter already produces,
195	  and should restrict `--cwd`/launch directory the same way design sessions
196	  restrict `workdir` to a configured allowlist
197	  [admin/server.py:81-101], rather than accepting an arbitrary path from the
198	  browser.
199	- **Daemon-stop is scoped as a rare, heavily-gated action, not a routine
200	  control.** `claude daemon stop` affects every session the supervisor hosts,
201	  not just ones the Control Room started. It is exposed only as an explicit,
202	  separately confirmed action, defaults to `--keep-workers` (sessions survive
203	  and the next supervisor reconnects to them) unless the operator
204	  affirmatively also wants to end running sessions, and is not offered from
205	  any bulk or default control.
206	
207	## 4. Constraints
208	
209	- Extend `admin/server.py` and `admin/static/` additively. Do not modify
210	  `admin/opencode_client.py`, `scripts/supervise.py`, or any
211	  `/api/design-sessions*` behavior — that surface belongs to a different
212	  feature owner and this feature must not change its endpoints, Redis keys,
213	  or semantics.
214	- Drive `claude` exclusively via `subprocess`, matching
215	  `src/instrument/claude_adapter.py`'s existing pattern. No new network
216	  service, no daemon RPC client, no polling of an undocumented socket
217	  protocol — only the CLI surfaces named in section 2.
218	- Do not implement, expose, or imply a send-input/steer control for a running
219	  background session. If the CLI reference gains one in the future, treat
220	  that as new investigation, not something to anticipate now.
221	- Reuse `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` and its retained-history/`replay_complete`
222	  contract [admin/server.py:450-490] for background-session transcripts. Do
223	  not add a second SSE endpoint shape or a new frontend stream type.
224	- Reuse the loopback + same-origin + JSON + `Idempotency-Key` mutation guard
225	  [admin/server.py:104-178] for every new `POST` endpoint (start, stop,
226	  respawn, rm, daemon stop), exactly as `/api/design-sessions/*` already does.
227	- Every destructive action — `stop`/`kill`, `rm`, `daemon stop` — is a
228	  one-way door from the operator's perspective and requires an explicit
229	  confirmation step in the UI before the request is sent, matching the
230	  existing Interrupt confirmation pattern [admin/static/app.js:1284-1300].
231	  `respawn` is control but not destructive (conversation survives) and does
232	  not require the same confirmation weight, though it should still be a
233	  deliberate click, not a default action.
234	- `claude daemon stop` defaults to `--keep-workers`; only an explicit,
235	  separately labeled operator choice omits it and allows sessions to be
236	  killed along with the supervisor.
237	- Restrict where background sessions can be started to a configured directory
238	  allowlist, reusing the shape of the existing `workdirs` mapping
239	  [admin/server.py:81-101]. Never accept an arbitrary filesystem path from
240	  the browser as a launch `--cwd`.
241	- Reuse `_resolve_claude_model`
242	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] for model selection so background
243	  sessions and headless runs resolve framework model ids identically.
244	  `--advisor` is passed straight through as an optional string from a small
245	  fixed set (`fable`, `opus`, `sonnet`, or a full model id); do not build new
246	  advisor logic.
247	- No new build step, dependency, or frontend framework. Python + the existing
248	  vanilla JS/CSS static app remain the implementation surface, per the
249	  Control Room's existing constraints.
250	- Bound poll frequency, JSON body size, and log-tail size the same way
251	  `/api/design-sessions` already bounds request size and prompt length
252	  [admin/server.py:66-67]; an unavailable `claude` binary or daemon must
253	  degrade to a visible error state, not hang the Flask request thread.
254	
255	## 5. Acceptance Criteria
256	
257	1. [ ] `admin/claude_agents_client.py` wraps `claude agents --json --all`,
258	   `claude --bg`, `claude logs <id>`, `claude stop <id>`,
259	   `claude respawn <id>`, `claude rm <id>`, and `claude daemon status` /
260	   `claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]` as subprocess calls, each
261	   returning parsed JSON or raw text plus a distinguishable error for a
262	   missing binary, non-zero exit, or timeout.
263	2. [ ] `GET /api/claude-agents` returns the cached/refreshed roster from
264	   `claude agents --json --all` (id, status, task/title, model, cwd,
265	   started/updated timestamps) without blocking on a live CLI call for every
266	   request.
267	3. [ ] `POST /api/claude-agents` starts a session via `claude --bg`, accepts
268	   only a workdir key from the configured allowlist (never a raw path),
269	   resolves the requested model through `_resolve_claude_model`, accepts an
270	   optional `--advisor` value from the fixed set, enforces the loopback/JSON/
271	   Idempotency-Key guard, and returns the new session id.
272	4. [ ] A background session's transcript is exposed through the existing
273	   `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` endpoint under a `claude_bg_<id>` cell id fed
274	   by a `claude logs <id>`-polling relay; no new SSE route or event schema is
275	   added, and the existing `replay_complete` boundary behavior is unchanged
276	   for both existing and new cell ids.
277	5. [ ] `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/stop` (aliasing `kill`) requires the
278	   mutation guard, requires the caller to have gone through an explicit
279	   confirmation step client-side, and reports whether the CLI accepted the
280	   stop.
281	6. [ ] `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/respawn` restarts the session and the
282	   response/roster reflects that its conversation id is unchanged.
283	7. [ ] `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/rm` requires confirmation, removes the
284	   session from the roster, and the response/UI states plainly that the

286	8. [ ] `GET /api/claude-agents/daemon` returns `claude daemon status` output

289	9. [ ] `POST /api/claude-agents/daemon/stop` is a separate, explicitly

291	   the operator has made an additional, distinct choice to also end running
292	   sessions; the UI states that this affects every session the supervisor
293	   hosts, not just ones started from the Control Room.
294	10. [ ] No endpoint, UI control, or client method sends input to, prompts,

2	
3	The Control Room backend uses raw HTTP because it is already a Python process;

5	API guarantees.  The browser never receives the OpenCode server address.
6	"""

42	    def __init__(self, base_url: str, *, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:

44	        self.timeout = timeout

46	    def _json_request(
47	        self,
48	        method: str,
49	        path: str,
50	        body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
51	        *,
52	        allow_empty: bool = False,
53	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
54	        """Issue one bounded JSON request and reject malformed success bodies."""
55	        payload = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
56	        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
57	        if payload is not None:
58	            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
59	        request = Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=payload, headers=headers, method=method)
60	        try:
61	            with urlopen(request, timeout=self.timeout) as response:  # noqa: S310 - configured loopback service

69	        except (URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:

76	        try:

105	        """Request interruption of active work without detaching the browser."""
106	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
107	        return self._json_request("POST", f"/api/session/{encoded}/interrupt", {}, allow_empty=True)
108	
109	    def messages(self, session_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
110	        """Return the native projected message history for explicit recovery."""
111	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
112	        return self._json_request("GET", f"/api/session/{encoded}/message")
113	
114	    def iter_events(self, session_id: str, *, after: str | None = None) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
115	        """Yield JSON objects from one native durable SSE subscription.
116	
117	        SSE ``id`` is retained as ``_sse_id`` when the JSON body does not carry
118	        an aggregate sequence.  Multi-line data fields are joined according to
119	        the SSE framing rules, while comments and unknown fields are ignored.
120	        """
121	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
122	        query = f"?{urlencode({'after': after})}" if after else ""
123	        request = Request(
124	            f"{self.base_url}/api/session/{encoded}/event{query}",
125	            headers={"Accept": "text/event-stream"},
126	            method="GET",
127	        )
128	        try:
129	            response = urlopen(request, timeout=max(self.timeout, 65.0))  # noqa: S310 - configured service
130	        except HTTPError as error:
131	            detail = error.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
132	            raise OpenCodeError(
133	                f"OpenCode event stream failed ({error.code}): {detail or error.reason}",
134	                error.code,
135	            ) from error
136	        except (URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:
137	            raise OpenCodeError(f"OpenCode event stream is unavailable: {error}") from error
138	
139	        content_type = response.headers.get_content_type()
140	        if content_type != "text/event-stream":
141	            response.close()
142	            raise OpenCodeError(f"OpenCode event stream returned {content_type}, not text/event-stream")
143	
144	        data_lines: list[str] = []
145	        data_size = 0
146	        event_id: str | None = None
147	        try:
148	            for raw_line in response:
149	                line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\r\n")
150	                if line == "":
151	                    if data_lines:
152	                        raw_data = "\n".join(data_lines)
153	                        try:
154	                            event = json.loads(raw_data)
155	                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
156	                            event = {"type": "raw", "data": raw_data}
157	                        if not isinstance(event, dict):
158	                            event = {"type": "raw", "data": event}
159	                        if event_id and not any(key in event for key in ("sequence", "aggregateSequence")):
160	                            event["_sse_id"] = event_id
161	                        yield event
162	                    data_lines = []
163	                    data_size = 0
164	                    event_id = None
165	                    continue
166	                if line.startswith(":"):
167	                    continue
168	                field, _, value = line.partition(":")
169	                value = value[1:] if value.startswith(" ") else value
170	                if field == "data":
171	                    data_lines.append(value)
172	                    data_size += len(value.encode(errors="replace"))
173	                    if data_size > MAX_SSE_EVENT_BYTES:
174	                        raise OpenCodeError("OpenCode SSE event exceeded the 2000000-byte limit")
175	                elif field == "id":
176	                    event_id = value
177	        finally:
178	            response.close()

81	def active_sessions(client: OpenCodeClient, *, skip: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:

83	    resp = client._json_request("GET", "/api/session", None)

97	def _text_from_messages(resp: dict, limit: int) -> str:
98	    """Flatten recent message texts into a compact string."""
99	    lines: list[str] = []
100	    for m in (resp.get("data") or resp.get("messages") or [])[-limit:]:
101	        role = m.get("role", "?")
102	        for part in (m.get("parts") or m.get("content") or []):
103	            if isinstance(part, str):
104	                text = part
105	            elif isinstance(part, dict):
106	                text = part.get("text") or part.get("reasoning") or ""
107	            else:
108	                text = ""
109	            if text:
110	                lines.append(f"{role}: {text[:200]}")

114	def read_reply(client: OpenCodeClient, session_id: str, *, wait_s: float = 60.0) -> str:
115	    """Poll the monitor's messages until a new assistant reply appears (best-effort)."""
116	    deadline = time.time() + wait_s
117	    last = ""
118	    while time.time() < deadline:
119	        try:
120	            resp = client.messages(session_id)
121	        except OpenCodeError:
122	            time.sleep(5)
123	            continue
124	        parts = resp.get("data") or resp.get("messages") or []
125	        if parts:
126	            last_msg = parts[-1]
127	            role = last_msg.get("role", "")
128	            for part in (last_msg.get("parts") or last_msg.get("content") or []):
129	                text = part.get("text") if isinstance(part, dict) else part
130	                if role == "assistant" and text and text.strip() != last:
131	                    return text
132	        time.sleep(5)
133	    return ""

136	def parse_verdict(reply: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
137	    status, why = "unknown", reply.strip()[:200] or "(no reply)"
138	    for line in reply.splitlines():
139	        if line.upper().startswith("STATUS:"):
140	            status = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip().lower()
141	        elif line.upper().startswith("WHY:"):
142	            why = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
143	    return status, why

146	def _slugify(value: str) -> str:
147	    out = "".join(ch if ch.isalnum() else "_" for ch in value).strip("_").lower()
148	    return out[:50] or "session"

151	def _cell_id_for(session: dict) -> str:
152	    """A readable Redis cell id for a native session, e.g. live_gpt_5_6_sol_facelift."""
153	    model = (session.get("model") or {}).get("id", "?")
154	    title = session.get("title") or ""
155	    return f"live_{_slugify(model)}_{_slugify(title)}"

158	def _relay_session(client: OpenCodeClient, sid: str, cell_id: str) -> None:
159	    """Stream one native session's durable events into Redis until it ends.
160	
161	    A full-history replay on first connect is acceptable: LivePublisher caps the
162	    retained list (ltrim), so the burst is bounded, and the Control Room's terminal
163	    replays the same retained window. After replay the stream goes live.
164	    """
165	    publisher = LivePublisher(cell_id)
166	    if publisher.enabled:
167	        publisher.set_status("running")
168	    try:
169	        for ev in client.iter_events(sid):
170	            publisher.publish_event(ev)
171	    except OpenCodeError:
172	        pass
173	    finally:
174	        if publisher.enabled:
175	            publisher.set_status("done")
176	
177	
178	def relay_once(client: OpenCodeClient, threads: dict[str, threading.Thread], finished: set[str]) -> None:
179	    """Maintain one persistent relay thread per active native session."""
180	    if not RELAY:
181	        return
182	    active = {s["id"]: s for s in active_sessions(client)}
183	    for sid, s in active.items():
184	        if sid in threads or sid in finished:
185	            continue
186	        cell_id = _cell_id_for(s)
187	        t = threading.Thread(target=_relay_session, args=(client, sid, cell_id), daemon=True)
188	        t.start()
189	        threads[sid] = t
190	    for sid in list(threads):
191	        if not threads[sid].is_alive():
192	            del threads[sid]
193	            finished.add(sid)
194	
195	
196	def emit_flag(session: dict, status: str, why: str) -> None:
197	    flag = {
198	        "at": now(),
199	        "session_id": session.get("id", ""),
200	        "title": session.get("title", "")[:80],
201	        "model": (session.get("model") or {}).get("id", "?"),
202	        "status": status,
203	        "why": why,
204	    }
205	    FLAGS_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
206	    with open(FLAGS_FILE, "a") as f:
207	        f.write(json.dumps(flag) + "\n")
208	    print(f"[FLAG] {status}: {flag['title']} — {why}", flush=True)
209	
210	
211	def supervise_once(client: OpenCodeClient, monitor_id: str, location: str) -> None:
212	    sessions = active_sessions(client, skip=monitor_id)
213	    if not sessions:
214	        log("no active sessions")
215	        return
216	    for s in sessions:
217	        sid = s.get("id", "")
218	        title = s.get("title", "")[:60]
219	        try:
220	            msgs = client.messages(sid)
221	        except OpenCodeError:
222	            continue
223	        text = _text_from_messages(msgs, BATCH_EVENTS)
224	        if not text.strip():
225	            continue
226	        batch = (
227	            f"SESSION: {title}\n"
228	            f"MODEL: {(s.get('model') or {}).get('id', '?')}\n"
229	            f"RECENT ACTIVITY (newest last):\n{text}\n\n"
230	            "Assess and reply STATUS + WHY."
231	        )
232	        try:
233	            client.send_input(monitor_id, batch, delivery="queue")
234	            reply = read_reply(client, monitor_id, wait_s=45.0)
235	        except OpenCodeError as e:
236	            log(f"monitor error for {title}: {e}")
237	            continue
238	        status, why = parse_verdict(reply)
239	        if status not in ("healthy", "unknown"):
240	            emit_flag(s, status, why)
241	
242	
243	def main() -> None:
244	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Flash session supervisor — flag only, never steer.")
245	    ap.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="run one assessment pass and exit")
246	    ap.add_argument("--location", default=str(ROOT), help="repo location for the monitor session")
247	    args = ap.parse_args()
248	
249	    client = OpenCodeClient(BASE_URL)
250	    monitor_id = ensure_monitor(client, args.location)
251	    threads: dict[str, threading.Thread] = {}
252	    finished: set[str] = set()
253	    log(f"relaying + monitoring (assess every {POLL_INTERVAL}s); flags -> {FLAGS_FILE}")
254	
255	    last_assess = 0.0
256	    while True:
257	        try:
258	            relay_once(client, threads, finished)
259	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
260	            log(f"relay error: {e!r}")
261	        if time.time() - last_assess >= POLL_INTERVAL:
262	            try:
263	                supervise_once(client, monitor_id, args.location)
264	            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
265	                log(f"error: {e!r}")
266	            last_assess = time.time()
267	        if args.once:
268	            return
269	        time.sleep(2)
270	
271	
272	if __name__ == "__main__":
273	    main()

2

4	provider layer. This module sidesteps that by driving the official ``claude``
5	CLI directly (``--output-format stream-json``) and translating its event
6	stream into opencode's ``run --format json`` event schema, so every downstream
7	parser (``analyze_trajectories``, ``efficiency``, lab books) works unchanged.
8	
9	Translation is stateful: Claude splits a tool call into an ``assistant``
10	``tool_use`` block (running) and a ``user`` ``tool_result`` block (done), while
11	opencode emits a single completed ``tool_use`` event. ``ClaudeStreamAdapter``
12	buffers pending calls and flushes one event per completed tool.
13	"""

49	def adapt_usage(usage: Any, total_cost_usd: float = 0.0) -> dict[str, Any]:
50	    """Map Claude CLI ``result.usage`` to opencode's ``step-finish`` tokens.
51	
52	    Claude does not break out reasoning tokens in usage (thinking is folded
53	    into ``output_tokens``), so ``reasoning`` is always 0 — matching the
54	    framework's honest-token semantics. Cache fields map directly.
55	    """
56	    if not isinstance(usage, dict):
57	        usage = {}
58	    input_tokens = int(usage.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0)
59	    output_tokens = int(usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0)
60	    cache_read = int(usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
61	    cache_write = int(usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
62	    total = input_tokens + output_tokens
63	    return {
64	        "tokens": {
65	            "input": input_tokens,
66	            "output": output_tokens,
67	            "reasoning": 0,
68	            "total": total,
69	            "cache": {"read": cache_read, "write": cache_write},
70	        },
71	        "cost": float(total_cost_usd or 0.0),
72	    }
73	
74	
75	class ClaudeStreamAdapter:
76	    """Stateful translator from Claude CLI stream-json events to opencode events."""
77	
78	    def __init__(self) -> None:
79	        self._pending_tools: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
80	        self._started = False
81	
82	    def feed(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
83	        """Translate one Claude event; returns zero or more opencode events."""
84	        etype = event.get("type", "")
85	
86	        if etype == "system":
87	            if self._started:
88	                return []
89	            self._started = True
90	            return [{"type": "step_start", "part": {"type": "step-start"}}]
91	
92	        if etype == "assistant":
93	            return self._handle_assistant(event.get("message", {}))
94	
95	        if etype == "user":
96	            return self._handle_user(event.get("message", {}))
97	
98	        if etype == "result":
99	            return self._handle_result(event)
100	
101	        return []
102	
103	    def _handle_assistant(self, message: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
104	        out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
105	        content = message.get("content", [])
106	        if not isinstance(content, list):
107	            content = []
108	        for block in content:
109	            if not isinstance(block, dict):
110	                continue
111	            btype = block.get("type")
112	            if btype == "text":
113	                text = block.get("text", "")
114	                if text:
115	                    out.append({"type": "text", "part": {"type": "text", "text": text}})
116	            elif btype == "thinking":
117	                text = block.get("thinking", "")
118	                if text:
119	                    out.append({"type": "reasoning", "part": {"type": "reasoning", "text": text}})
120	            elif btype == "tool_use":
121	                call_id = block.get("id", "")
122	                self._pending_tools[call_id] = {
123	                    "tool": block.get("name", ""),
124	                    "input": block.get("input", {}),
125	                }
126	        return out
127	
128	    def _handle_user(self, message: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
129	        out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
130	        content = message.get("content", [])
131	        if not isinstance(content, list):
132	            content = []
133	        for block in content:
134	            if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "tool_result":
135	                continue
136	            call_id = block.get("tool_use_id", "")
137	            pending = self._pending_tools.pop(call_id, {"tool": "", "input": {}})
138	            status = "error" if block.get("is_error") else "completed"
139	            out.append(
140	                {
141	                    "type": "tool_use",
142	                    "part": {
143	                        "type": "tool",
144	                        "tool": pending["tool"],
145	                        "callID": call_id,
146	                        "state": {
147	                            "status": status,
148	                            "input": pending["input"],
149	                            "output": block.get("content", ""),
150	                        },
151	                    },
152	                }
153	            )
154	        return out
155	
156	    def _handle_result(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
157	        out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
158	        for call_id, pending in self._pending_tools.items():
159	            out.append(
160	                {
161	                    "type": "tool_use",
162	                    "part": {
163	                        "type": "tool",
164	                        "tool": pending["tool"],
165	                        "callID": call_id,
166	                        "state": {"status": "completed", "input": pending["input"], "output": ""},
167	                    },
168	                }
169	            )
170	        self._pending_tools.clear()
171	
172	        usage = adapt_usage(event.get("usage", {}), event.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0))
173	        out.append(
174	            {
175	                "type": "step_finish",
176	                "part": {"type": "step-finish", "tokens": usage["tokens"], "cost": usage["cost"]},
177	            }
178	        )
179	        return out

236	def run_claude_agentic(
237	    prompt: str,
238	    *,
239	    model: str = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
240	    thinking_effort: str | None = None,
241	    thinking_budget_tokens: int = 0,
242	    output_token_limit: int = 0,
243	    silent_mode: bool | None = None,
244	    standardize: bool = True,
245	    enforce_pytest: bool = True,
246	    workdir: str | None = None,
247	    timeout: int = 300,
248	    session_name: str = "",
249	    init_git: bool = True,
250	    on_event: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
251	    transcript_path: str | None = None,
252	) -> AgenticResult:
253	    """Run an agentic session through the Claude CLI, emitting opencode JSONL.
254	
255	    Mirrors ``run_opencode_agentic``: same worktree isolation, standardized
256	    prompt injection, and ``AgenticResult`` return — but execution happens in
257	    the official ``claude`` CLI and its stream is translated to opencode's
258	    event schema.
259	
260	    Note: Claude CLI exposes no reasoning-effort flag; thinking is constrained
261	    by the standardized prompt header (``thinking_budget_tokens``), matching
262	    the opencode path.
263	    """
264	    import tempfile
265	
266	    t0 = time.monotonic()
267	    result = AgenticResult(
268	        run_id=session_name or f"claude_{int(t0)}", task=prompt, model=model, workdir=workdir
269	    )
270	    result.thinking_effort = thinking_effort or "default"
271	    result.thinking_budget_tokens = thinking_budget_tokens
272	
273	    if standardize and not prompt.startswith("[STANDARDIZED CONSTRAINTS"):
274	        prompt = _build_standardized_prompt(
275	            prompt,
276	            thinking_budget_tokens=thinking_budget_tokens,
277	            output_token_limit=output_token_limit,
278	            enforce_pytest=enforce_pytest,
279	            silent_mode=silent_mode,
280	        )
281	
282	    if workdir is None:
283	        workdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="exp_")
284	        result.workdir = workdir
285	
286	    if init_git:
287	        _init_git_workdir(workdir)
288	
289	    files_before = _list_files(workdir)
290	
291	    cmd = [
292	        CLAUDE_BIN,
293	        "-p",
294	        prompt,
295	        "--output-format",
296	        "stream-json",
297	        "--verbose",
298	        "--dangerously-skip-permissions",
299	    ]
300	    cmd.extend(_claude_model_arg(model))
301	
302	    adapter = ClaudeStreamAdapter()
303	    translated_lines: list[str] = []
304	    publisher = make_publisher() if on_event is None else None
305	
306	    def on_line(line: str) -> None:
307	        try:
308	            event = json.loads(line)
309	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
310	            return
311	        for out in adapter.feed(event):
312	            translated_lines.append(json.dumps(out))
313	            if on_event is not None:
314	                on_event(out)
315	            elif publisher is not None:
316	                publisher.publish_event(out)
317	
318	    stream = stream_subprocess(cmd, workdir=workdir, timeout=timeout, on_line=on_line)
319	
320	    if stream.timed_out:
321	        result.error = f"Timeout after {timeout}s"
322	        result.exit_code = -1
323	    else:
324	        result.exit_code = stream.exit_code
325	        result.error = stream.stderr.strip() if stream.exit_code != 0 else ""
326	
327	    result.raw_transcript = "\n".join(translated_lines)
328	    if result.raw_transcript:
329	        _parse_session_output(result.raw_transcript, result)
330	
331	    result.duration_s = time.monotonic() - t0
332	    result.files_created, result.files_modified = _diff_workdir(workdir, files_before)
333	
334	    if result.estimated_cost_usd <= 0 and result.total_tokens > 0:
335	        result.estimated_cost_usd = _estimate_claude_cost(result, model)
336	
337	    if result.raw_transcript:
338	        out_path = (
339	            Path(transcript_path)
340	            if transcript_path
341	            else Path(workdir) / ".instrument" / "session.jsonl"
342	        )
343	        out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
344	        out_path.write_text(result.raw_transcript)
345	
346	    return result

127	def _idempotent_design_response(
128	    operation: str, body: dict, action
129	) -> tuple[Response, int] | Response:
130	    """Reserve and replay one JSON mutation result using Redis atomic ``SET NX``."""
131	    supplied_key = request.headers["Idempotency-Key"]
132	    request_digest = hashlib.sha256(
133	        json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
134	    ).hexdigest()
135	    cache_id = hashlib.sha256(f"{operation}\0{supplied_key}".encode()).hexdigest()
136	    cache_key = f"control_room:idempotency:{cache_id}"
137	    reservation = json.dumps({"state": "pending", "request_digest": request_digest})
138	    try:
139	        redis_client = _redis()
140	        reserved = redis_client.set(
141	            cache_key,
142	            reservation,
143	            nx=True,
144	            ex=IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS,
145	        )
146	        if not reserved:
147	            existing_raw = redis_client.get(cache_key)
148	            existing = json.loads(existing_raw) if existing_raw else {}
149	            if existing.get("request_digest") != request_digest:
150	                return (
151	                    jsonify({"error": "Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request"}),
152	                    409,
153	                )
154	            if existing.get("state") == "complete":
155	                return jsonify(existing.get("body", {})), int(existing.get("status", 200))
156	            return (
157	                jsonify({"error": "matching mutation is still in progress", "retryable": True}),
158	                409,
159	            )
160	    except Exception as error:
161	        return jsonify({"error": f"idempotency store unavailable: {error}"}), 503
162	
163	    try:
164	        response = make_response(action())
165	    except Exception as error:
166	        response = make_response(_design_error(error))
167	    completed = json.dumps({
168	        "state": "complete",
169	        "request_digest": request_digest,
170	        "status": response.status_code,
171	        "body": response.get_json(silent=True) or {},
172	    })
173	    with suppress(Exception):
174	        redis_client.set(cache_key, completed, ex=IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS)
175	    # The action already completed. A cache-write failure must not invite a
176	    # new-key retry that duplicates paid or filesystem-changing work.
177	    return response

234	def _step_sample(payload) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
235	    """Extract one defensive token/cost sample from a raw event payload.
236	
237	    Both current events (fields under ``part``) and retained legacy events
238	    (top-level fields) are supported. A step with no valid token or cost value
239	    is omitted because it cannot contribute to a chart or aggregate.
240	    """
241	    try:
242	        event = json.loads(payload) if isinstance(payload, str) else payload
243	    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
244	        return None
245	    if not isinstance(event, dict):
246	        return None
247	
248	    event_type = str(event.get("type", "")).replace("-", "_").lower()
249	    if event_type != "step_finish":
250	        return None
251	    part = event.get("part") if isinstance(event.get("part"), dict) else event
252	    tokens = part.get("tokens") if isinstance(part.get("tokens"), dict) else {}
253	
254	    input_tokens = _reported_number(tokens.get("input"))
255	    output_tokens = _reported_number(tokens.get("output"))
256	    reasoning_tokens = _reported_number(tokens.get("reasoning"))
257	    total_tokens = _reported_number(tokens.get("total"))
258	    cache = tokens.get("cache")
259	    cache_tokens = _reported_number(cache)
260	    if isinstance(cache, dict):
261	        cache_values = [_reported_number(cache.get("read")), _reported_number(cache.get("write"))]
262	        valid_cache = [value for value in cache_values if value is not None]
263	        cache_tokens = sum(valid_cache) if valid_cache else None
264	
265	    # Some providers omit ``total``. Summing only explicitly reported fields
266	    # yields a useful bar without manufacturing missing token values as zero.
267	    if total_tokens is None:
268	        components = [input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cache_tokens]
269	        reported_components = [value for value in components if value is not None]
270	        total_tokens = sum(reported_components) if reported_components else None
271	
272	    cost = _reported_number(part.get("cost"))
273	    if cost is None and total_tokens is None:
274	        return None
275	
276	    timestamp = _event_timestamp(event, part)
277	    session_id = event.get("sessionID") or part.get("sessionID")
278	    identity = "|".join([
279	        str(session_id or ""),
280	        str(timestamp if timestamp is not None else ""),
281	        _identity_number(cost),
282	        _identity_number(input_tokens),
283	        _identity_number(output_tokens),
284	        _identity_number(reasoning_tokens),
285	        _identity_number(cache_tokens),
286	        _identity_number(total_tokens),
287	    ])
288	    return {
289	        "identity": identity,
290	        "timestamp": timestamp,
291	        "cost": cost,
292	        "input_tokens": input_tokens,
293	        "output_tokens": output_tokens,
294	        "reasoning_tokens": reasoning_tokens,
295	        "cache_tokens": cache_tokens,
296	        "total_tokens": total_tokens,
297	    }

300	def _retained_telemetry(redis_client, cell_ids) -> dict[str, Any]:
301	    """Build an additive retained-window snapshot from existing event logs.
302	
303	    Each log is independently optional. A transient per-cell read failure does
304	    not erase the baseline matrix response; ``available`` records that the
305	    telemetry extension is incomplete while the legacy status data remains
306	    usable.
307	
308	    All log reads are issued in a single non-transactional pipeline so the
309	    fleet snapshot costs one round trip, not one per cell.
310	    """
311	    cells = {}
312	    total_cost = 0.0
313	    input_tokens = 0.0
314	    output_tokens = 0.0
315	    cost_samples = input_samples = output_samples = 0
316	    available = True
317	    capped = False
318	
319	    keys = [f"{EVENT_LOG_PREFIX}{cell_id}" for cell_id in cell_ids]
320	    try:
321	        pipe = redis_client.pipeline(transaction=False)
322	        for key in keys:
323	            pipe.lrange(key, 0, -1)
324	        histories = pipe.execute()
325	    except Exception:
326	        # A connection-level failure marks telemetry incomplete but must not
327	        # erase the legacy matrix response (same contract as today).
328	        histories = [None] * len(cell_ids)
329	
330	    for cell_id, history in zip(cell_ids, histories):
331	        if history is None:
332	            available = False
333	            history = []
334	        capped = capped or len(history) >= EVENT_LOG_MAX
335	
336	        samples = []
337	        for payload in reversed(history):
338	            sample = _step_sample(payload)
339	            if sample is None:
340	                continue
341	            samples.append(sample)
342	            if sample["cost"] is not None:
343	                total_cost += sample["cost"]
344	                cost_samples += 1
345	            if sample["input_tokens"] is not None:
346	                input_tokens += sample["input_tokens"]
347	                input_samples += 1
348	            if sample["output_tokens"] is not None:
349	                output_tokens += sample["output_tokens"]
350	                output_samples += 1
351	
352	        cell_costs = [sample["cost"] for sample in samples if sample["cost"] is not None]
353	        cell_inputs = [
354	            sample["input_tokens"] for sample in samples if sample["input_tokens"] is not None
355	        ]
356	        cell_outputs = [
357	            sample["output_tokens"] for sample in samples if sample["output_tokens"] is not None
358	        ]
359	        cells[cell_id] = {
360	            "reported_cost": sum(cell_costs) if cell_costs else None,
361	            "input_tokens": sum(cell_inputs) if cell_inputs else None,
362	            "output_tokens": sum(cell_outputs) if cell_outputs else None,
363	            "latest_cost": cell_costs[-1] if cell_costs else None,
364	            "samples": samples,
365	            "history_size": len(history),
366	            "history_capped": len(history) >= EVENT_LOG_MAX,
367	            "partial": True,
368	        }
369	
370	    return {
371	        "available": available,
372	        "provenance": "retained_window",
373	        "partial": True,
374	        "reported_cost": total_cost if cost_samples else None,
375	        "input_tokens": input_tokens if input_samples else None,
376	        "output_tokens": output_tokens if output_samples else None,
377	        "cost_samples": cost_samples,
378	        "history_capped": capped,
379	        "cells": cells,
380	    }

"""Live telemetry — Redis Pub/Sub publisher for background experiment progress.

No-ops gracefully when Redis is unavailable or ``FINOPS_CELL_ID`` is unset, so
an experiment run never fails because the dashboard is down. Channels mirror
``scripts/monitor.py``:

    - status hash:      ``story_status``         (cell_id -> queued|running|done|failed|timeout)
    - pub/sub channel:  ``status``               (status transitions)
    - pub/sub channel:  ``events:{cell_id}``     (per-cell session event stream)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from typing import Any

REDIS_HOST = os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
REDIS_PORT = int(os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_PORT", "6380"))
REDIS_DB = int(os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_DB", "1"))
STATUS_KEY = "story_status"
STATUS_CHANNEL = "status"
EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX = "events:"
EVENT_LOG_PREFIX = "events_log:"
EVENT_LOG_MAX = 500


def _connect() -> Any:
    """Connect to Redis, returning None if unavailable (never raises)."""
    try:
        import redis

        r = redis.Redis(
            host=REDIS_HOST,
            port=REDIS_PORT,
            db=REDIS_DB,
            decode_responses=True,
            socket_connect_timeout=2,
            socket_keepalive=False,
        )
        r.ping()
        return r
    except Exception:
        return None


class LivePublisher:
    """Publish live experiment progress to Redis Pub/Sub.

    Disables itself permanently after the first failure so a downed Redis
    server costs one attempt, not one per event.
    """

    def __init__(self, cell_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.cell_id = cell_id or os.environ.get("FINOPS_CELL_ID", "").strip()
        self._r = _connect() if self.cell_id else None
        self._disabled = self._r is None

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        return not self._disabled and bool(self.cell_id)

    def publish_status(self, status: str) -> None:
        """Publish a cell status transition to the ``status`` channel."""
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        try:
            self._r.publish(STATUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps({"cell_id": self.cell_id, "status": status}))
        except Exception:
            self._disabled = True

    def set_status(self, status: str) -> None:
        """Record status in the ``story_status`` hash AND publish the transition.

        The portal's fleet reads the hash (``GET /api/matrix``); the live stream reads
        the channel (``GET /api/status``). Both must be updated for a cell to appear.
        """
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        try:
            self._r.hset(STATUS_KEY, self.cell_id, status)
            self._r.publish(STATUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps({"cell_id": self.cell_id, "status": status}))
        except Exception:
            self._disabled = True

    def publish_event(self, event: dict[str, Any] | str) -> None:
        """Publish a single session event to ``events:{cell_id}``.

        Also appends to a bounded history list (``events_log:{cell_id}``) so a
        portal can replay the tail before subscribing — Redis pub/sub has no
        message history.
        """
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        payload = event if isinstance(event, str) else json.dumps(event)
        channel = f"{EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX}{self.cell_id}"
        log_key = f"{EVENT_LOG_PREFIX}{self.cell_id}"
        try:
            # Persist before publishing so "delivered live" implies "already
            # retained": a poll that starts after a publish is guaranteed to
            # observe the entry (or it was evicted from the shared bounded
            # window, which the fleet flag labels). The reverse failure mode
            # (lpush succeeds, publish fails) degrades to a bounded poll pickup.
            self._r.lpush(log_key, payload)
            self._r.ltrim(log_key, 0, EVENT_LOG_MAX - 1)
            self._r.publish(channel, payload)
        except Exception:
            self._disabled = True


def make_publisher() -> LivePublisher | None:
    """Return a LivePublisher for the current cell, or None if disabled.

    Driven by the ``FINOPS_CELL_ID`` env var (set by the experiment worker so
    every backend session in the process tree publishes to the right cell).
    """
    cell_id = os.environ.get("FINOPS_CELL_ID", "").strip()
    if not cell_id:
        return None
    return LivePublisher(cell_id)

# Challenge: Claude Code Background Sessions Scope

Reviewed against `docs/scope.md`, the code it cites
(`admin/opencode_client.py`, `scripts/supervise.py`, `admin/server.py`,
`src/instrument/claude_adapter.py`, `admin/design_sessions.py`,
`admin/static/app.js`), and the live Claude Code CLI reference
(`https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference`), fetched directly for this
review rather than taken on faith.

## 0. CLI facts: verified accurate

Section 2's quoted commands and flags (`--bg`/`--background`, `claude
agents`/`--json`/`--all`/`--cwd`, `claude attach`, `claude logs`, `claude
daemon status`, `claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]`, `claude
stop`/`kill`, `claude respawn [--all]`, `claude rm`, `--advisor <model>`) were
re-fetched from the live reference for this review and match the scope
document essentially verbatim, including the "requires an interactive
terminal" caveat on `claude agents` and the "recent output" wording on
`claude logs`. The document's central claim — that the CLI is a documented,
scriptable contract for everything except send-input/steer — holds up. This
matters because the whole feature stands or falls on that contract being
right, and it is.

## 1. Where I agree

- **No invented steer/interrupt.** The CLI has no equivalent to OpenCode's
  `delivery: queue|steer` [admin/opencode_client.py:94-102], and the scope
  correctly refuses to fake one via subprocess stdin. This also matches the
  repo's own existing philosophy: `scripts/supervise.py`'s monitor is
  explicitly "flags only. A human decides the intervention"
  [scripts/supervise.py:9,48]. Not inventing a control the vendor doesn't
  document is the right call, not just a cautious one.
- **`claude logs` over `claude attach`/`claude agents` for headless
  polling.** Both of the latter are documented as needing a real TTY; `logs`
  is a plain stdout dump. Driving only the scriptable subset via subprocess
  is consistent with how `claude_adapter.py` already drives the CLI
  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299].
- **Reusing `GET /api/events/<cell_id>` under a `claude_bg_<id>` cell
  namespace** instead of a new SSE shape is the same trick
  `scripts/supervise.py` already uses for OpenCode (`_cell_id_for`,
  [scripts/supervise.py:151-155]) and it's the right one here too — zero new
  frontend stream types.
- **Daemon-stop defaulting to `--keep-workers`, gated separately from
  routine controls.** `daemon stop` is documented as affecting every session
  the supervisor hosts, not just Control-Room-started ones, and scoping it as
  a rare, explicitly-confirmed action with a safe default is proportionate to
  that blast radius.
- **Reusing `_resolve_claude_model` and the workdir-allowlist shape**
  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211; admin/server.py:81-101] instead
  of building parallel model-resolution or path-validation logic is the
  correct anti-duplication call, and it's consistent with how
  `admin/design_sessions.py` already restricts `workdir_key` to an approved
  map [admin/design_sessions.py:284-288].
- **Reusing the loopback + JSON + Idempotency-Key mutation guard**
  [admin/server.py:104-124] for every new `POST` route rather than writing a
  second guard is correct; it's exactly what `/api/design-sessions/*` already
  does for every mutating endpoint.

## 2. Where I disagree

### 2.1 The roster is host-wide, not Control-Room-owned — this is a safety gap, not a detail

`claude agents --json --all` lists **every** background session on the
machine, including ones an operator started by hand in a terminal, unrelated
to the Control Room. The scope's acceptance criteria (#2) only says the
roster comes from that call; nothing scopes it to sessions the Control Room
itself launched. That means the fleet UI will show Stop/Respawn/Rm buttons —
one-way-door actions per the scope's own constraint — on sessions the
operator didn't start and may not know about, with no visual distinction.
Contrast this with the daemon-stop action, where the scope *does* explicitly
call out "affects every session the supervisor hosts, not just ones started
from the Control Room" (§3 Rationale, criterion 9) — the same reasoning
should apply to the plain roster list, and it doesn't.

**Alternative:** query `claude agents --cwd <path> --json --all` once per
configured workdir-allowlist entry (the CLI supports exactly this scoping
flag) instead of one unscoped `--all` call, and additionally track
Control-Room-launched session ids in a small Redis set written at `--bg`
start time. Render sessions found only via the `--cwd` scan but absent from
that set as "external — not started here," and require the strongest
confirmation copy (or disable Stop/Rm outright) for them. This costs one
Redis set and a few more `--cwd`-scoped calls; it does not touch the
`--all`-vs-scoped decision the daemon-stop rationale already implicitly
endorses.

### 2.2 Relaying only the *selected* session loses history the OpenCode side never loses

The decision routes log-diffing through "the currently selected/attached
session only" (§3 Decision). Compare `scripts/supervise.py`, which the scope
repeatedly cites as the pattern to mirror: `relay_once` maintains one relay
thread **per active session**, continuously, regardless of what's selected in
the UI [scripts/supervise.py:178-193]. That works for OpenCode because the
native server holds durable, gapless history independent of the Control
Room's polling — `iter_events` can always backfill full history on attach
[admin/opencode_client.py:114-137]. `claude logs <id>` has no such backing
store from the Control Room's point of view: the reference describes it as
"recent output," i.e. a bounded tail, not a durable full-history API. Combine
those two facts and a session that runs for a while before anyone selects its
card can have its early output permanently unrecoverable — there is no
retained window for a cell nobody was polling, and by the time it's selected
`claude logs` may no longer have the early lines to backfill from.

**Alternative:** mirror `relay_once`'s actual behavior, not just its naming
convention — start a `claude logs`-diffing thread for every session returned
by the roster poll (bounded by the same `--cwd` scoping from 2.1), not just
the selected one, so retained history accumulates in Redis the same way it
does for OpenCode regardless of UI attention. If the resource cost of N
concurrent polling threads is the actual reason for the "selected only"
choice, say so explicitly and put a number on it (max concurrent relays,
poll interval) rather than leaving "selected only" implicit — either way,
acceptance criterion 4 should state plainly that Claude transcripts are
best-effort/tail-bounded, not the gapless equivalent OpenCode gets, so nobody
mistakes the "reuses the same SSE endpoint" plumbing for "reuses the same
fidelity guarantee."

### 2.3 Embedding subprocess polling in the Flask dev server risks the resource the docstring already warns about

`admin/server.py`'s own module docstring flags that `app.run(threaded=True)`
is "Flask's built-in single-process development server" and that every SSE
client "holds one request thread... for the life of the tab, so there is no
connection cap" [admin/server.py:16-20]. The scope's decision to add a
"module-level thread" that runs `claude agents --json --all` on an interval
plus (per 2.2, ideally N) `claude logs`-polling relay threads, each shelling
out via `subprocess`, adds more long-lived thread + blocking-subprocess
pressure to that same single process — on top of the SSE thread-per-tab load
the docstring already flags as needing a production gunicorn front-end for
multi-operator use. The scope explicitly rejects "a new always-on service"
(§3 Decision) without weighing this against the alternative the codebase
already has for exactly this shape of problem.

**Alternative:** give the poller/relay the same separate-process treatment
`scripts/supervise.py` already has for OpenCode, e.g.
`scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py`: it owns all `subprocess` calls to
`claude`, writes the roster and relayed log lines straight to Redis, and
`admin/server.py` only ever reads Redis for `GET /api/claude-agents*` — the
same read-only relationship `api_matrix`/`api_events` already have to
`scripts/supervise.py`'s output. `POST` actions (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon
stop) can stay synchronous subprocess calls inside Flask, since those are
short, bounded, one-shot commands, not long-lived polling loops — it's
specifically the *polling* that doesn't belong in the request-serving
process, not all subprocess use.

### 2.4 The Problem framing promises more than the Approach delivers, silently

The Problem section justifies this feature by pointing at "the Control
Room['s]... native supervisor surface for OpenCode," and names both halves
of it: `admin/opencode_client.py` (observe/control) *and*
`scripts/supervise.py`, described as flagging "stalled/off-track work for
human review" [docs/scope.md:5-8]. The Chosen Integration Approach then only
builds the `opencode_client.py`-equivalent half (list/observe/lifecycle
control) — there is no proposed equivalent to the flash-model monitor that
reads session activity and emits healthy/stalled/off_track flags. That may
well be the right phasing choice (get observe+control shipped first), but
the scope never says so — it cites the flagging behavior as motivation and
then quietly doesn't build it, which reads as an oversight rather than a
decision if a reader isn't cross-checking `scripts/supervise.py` themselves.
It's a real, buildable follow-on: `claude logs <id>` output is exactly the
kind of text `supervise_once`'s batching already knows how to summarize
[scripts/supervise.py:211-240], so nothing here is CLI-blocked.

**Alternative:** either trim the Problem section's framing to the half
actually being built (observe + lifecycle control), or add one sentence to
§3/§4 stating that AI-flagging of background-session health is explicitly
out of scope for this phase and left as a follow-up once `claude logs`
polling exists to feed it. Either fixes the mismatch; leaving it unstated
does not.

## 3. Recommendation

Proceed to the spec phase with the CLI contract and the observe/control
shape as scoped — but resolve 2.1 (roster ownership scoping) and 2.4
(explicit phasing of the flagging gap) in the spec itself before writing
acceptance criteria, since both change what "done" means; 2.2 and 2.3 are
implementation-shape calls that can be settled during spec or left as
explicit, documented trade-offs if the team prefers the simpler
selected-only/embedded-poller path.
